passage: On the whiteboard in the project lab, Rehana drew four boxes and started joining them with arrows. "Look," she said, tapping. "Nothing can train until the pipeline is running. So model training waits for Uday's pipeline. But the interface only needs a fake output for now, so Sharath can start it today." Uday, who owned the pipeline, glanced up from his laptop. "So I'm the bottleneck." "For a week or two, yes," said Rehana. "So the rest of us help you first: I'll write the cleaning script, Sharath will test the loader." She circled the pipeline box in red. "This is the critical path. If it slips, everything slips." Uday exhaled, and pulled a chair for Sharath.

qa.q: What is Uday feeling when Rehana says the pipeline is the critical path?
qa.a: Uday feels the pressure of being the bottleneck, then some relief as Uday exhales and pulls a chair for Sharath because help is coming.

qa.q: What alternative approach could the team use to avoid waiting on one person, and why?
qa.a: They could agree on a simple fake data file for the model people to use meanwhile, because parallel work continues even before the real pipeline is ready.

qa.q: How does Sharath see this plan?
qa.a: Sharath can start the interface today with a fake output and also helps by testing the loader, so Sharath is neither idle nor blocked.

grounding: Shows dependency thinking in a team: the pipeline must come first, other parts can run in parallel, and the pipeline owner gets help.

passage:
Subject: Changing our plan this week (please read before Friday)
Hi all,
I spent last night drawing our project as boxes and arrows, and I think we've been working in the wrong order.
Model training (Aman's part) can't start until the data pipeline (Binita's part) is working. No clean data, no model. The interface (mine and Ritika's) doesn't depend on either. We can build it with sample data now and plug the real model in later.
So the pipeline is the thing everything waits on. Right now Binita is doing it alone while three of us polish screens.
Proposal: for the next two weeks, Aman helps Binita with the pipeline, since he needs its output anyway. Ritika and I carry on with the interface in parallel. Once the pipeline runs, Aman switches to training.
Binita, does this help, or would you rather split it differently?
Dhruv

qa.q: Whose part is the data pipeline?

qa.a: Dhruv was worried the team had been working in the wrong order, leaving Binita alone on the part everything waits on.

qa.q: What else could help the pipeline move faster?
qa.a: The team could agree a simple sample data format early, so Aman can start testing small model pieces while the full pipeline is finished.

qa.q: How might Binita see the proposal?
qa.a: Binita, who has been doing the pipeline alone, would likely feel relieved and supported, and is invited to shape the split.

grounding: Shows a team member seeing that the data pipeline must come before model training while the interface can run in parallel, so the pipeline owner gets help first.

passage: Anjali, you asked why our team started helping Sohail in week five. I'm Irawati. Our project was a model that predicts crop prices, with a web interface. Four parts: data pipeline, model, interface, report. For a month, everyone worked on their own part. Then one night I drew it as a chain. The model needs cleaned data. The data needs Sohail's pipeline. So if Sohail is late, the model is late, and so is everything after it. But the interface? It only needs a sample output file. We could build it any time. That's when I saw that the pipeline was the one link nothing could skip. Everything else could wait; that couldn't. So I moved from the report, which had loads of slack, to help Sohail with data cleaning. Two weeks later the pipeline ran, and the model team finally had something real to train on.

qa.a: It only needs a sample output file.

qa.q: How did Irawati feel on drawing the chain?
qa.a: Irawati felt a flash of clarity, and some alarm, seeing that the whole project depended on Sohail's pipeline.

qa.q: What else could the team do once the pipeline runs?
qa.a: They could redraw the chain to find the next step everything depends on, such as model training, and move help there.

qa.q: How might Sohail have experienced the extra help?
qa.a: Sohail, likely under pressure as the part everyone waited on, probably felt relieved when Irawati joined.

grounding: Illustrates a student mapping which parts depend on which, seeing the data pipeline must come before training, and moving help to the pipeline.
